_comment: Registration for scripts/instrument-census-check.py (issue #1060).
WHY THIS GATE NEEDS A COMMITTED CASE (ADR 0008): it is a gate that lets work
THROUGH. `make verify` and the CI `instrument-census-check` step both read its
green as 'ADR 0008's census describes this tree', and nothing downstream
re-derives that. It is also the gate every OTHER coverage number rests on: the
denominator `check-negative-controls.py` prints is this table's row count, so a
blind version here makes the coverage fraction quietly wrong everywhere it is
quoted, including in release notes.
A blind version would print the same clean line over the pre-#1060 state, where
eight instruments were in neither table - among them counter-model-receipt.py,
which then shipped carrying #1047 and #1048, the exact defect class this table
exists to bound.
THE CASES ARE WHOLE FIXTURE TREES, not the real repository. The gate takes
--root, so a case is a miniature repo: a two- or three-script `scripts/` and a
small ADR with the real document's shape (numbered census rows, an 'Excluded,
with the reason' section, an external-subjects marker). Deliberately tiny - the
question is whether the gate can tell an accounted tree from an unaccounted one.
EACH BAD CASE FIRES EXACTLY ONE FINDING, and that cost a rewrite. The first cut
left an exclusion row naming `sandbox-trial.sh`, a file absent from the fixture
tree, so BOTH bad cases also reported an incidental STALE. Each would then have
scored BAD even with the direction it exists to prove completely removed - a case
that cannot fail for its own reason is not evidence about that reason.
TWO BAD CASES, because the gate draws two distinctions:
bad-unaccounted    a script in neither table - the drift #1060 is about, and
the shape that accumulated eight times unnoticed. The
fixture NAMES it in the document's prose, which is what
makes the anchor miss it rather than merely differ.
bad-stale-subject  a census row for a script that is not in the tree. The
forward check alone scores this clean, so without this case
the reverse direction ships unexercised and the denominator
can inflate silently - in the flattering direction.
The GOOD case exercises all three accounting paths, not just the census one:
`alpha-tool.sh` by a census row, `delta-tool.sh` by an exclusion, and `ruff` by
the external-subjects declaration. THE HALF THAT MATTERS for a gate wedged at
'fail': a check that refuses every tree is indistinguishable from a working one
on the bad cases alone, and this gate is in `make verify`, so a false red blocks
every merge in the repository.
Stdlib-only and git-free, like the gate: no binary this fixture needs is absent
from the slim CI image, so the control gives the same verdict there as here.
THE DATA HOME (issue #1671). The census moved out of ADR 0008 into
`controls/census.md`, and the gate now reads that file first. The four cases
above keep their census inside the decision record on purpose: that is still
a supported location (kyle keeps its census there), so they are the control
for the fallback, and the known-bad case #1060 committed is the one #1671's
acceptance names - run before and after the move, red both times.
Two more cases put the census where the real one now is, and each ALSO
carries a decision record that disagrees with it, so the cases discriminate
on precedence and not only on location:
bad-unaccounted-data-home   the data file omits `beta-tool.sh`; a leftover
table in the decision record accounts for it.
The pre-#1671 gate, which reads the record,
scores this tree clean (measured).
good-accounted-data-home    the data file is exact; the decision record
holds no table at all, the real record's shape
since #1671. The pre-#1671 gate parses 0 rows
and refuses this correct tree (measured).
good_signal: ^instrument-census-check: ok - all \d+ file\(s\) in scripts/ are accounted for by

cases.name: bad-unaccounted
cases.why: `beta-tool.sh` is named by no census row and no exclusion - the exact case issue #1060 requires committed. It IS named in the document's prose, so the rejected extraction rule (any backticked token anywhere) scores this tree clean. If this scores GOOD the gate cannot see an unenumerated instrument at all, which is the only thing it exists to see.

cases.name: bad-stale-subject
cases.why: The population is fully accounted for, but a census row survives for `gamma-tool.sh`, which is not in the tree. The forward check alone reports this tree clean. Without this case the reverse direction ships unexercised, and a census that keeps rows for deleted tooling inflates the denominator every coverage figure is quoted against.

cases.name: bad-stale-make-target
cases.why: A census row for `make nosuch` where the tree's Makefile defines only `verify` (#1276). Before #1276 every `make <target>` row read as the one subject `make`, and with `make` declared external this row resolved silently, so the census could keep describing a deleted Makefile gate forever. It is now the typed subject `make:nosuch`, validated against the Makefile, and STALE. The external `make` stays declared in this fixture precisely so the old reading had a way to pass.

cases.name: bad-unaccounted-data-home
cases.why: The #1060 known-bad shape at the census's home since #1671: `controls/census.md` names `beta-tool.sh` in prose and in no row or exclusion. The tree also holds a decision record whose leftover table DOES account for it, so a gate that still reads the record first scores this clean - measured against the pre-#1671 gate. If this scores GOOD, the gate is reading a census nobody maintains any more and an unenumerated instrument is invisible again.

cases.name: good-accounted
cases.why: A tree whose census matches it exactly, exercising all three accounting paths - a census row, an exclusion row, and a declared external subject. THE HALF THAT MATTERS for a gate wedged at 'fail': a check that refuses every tree passes both bad cases on its own, and this gate is in `make verify`, so a false red blocks every merge in the repository. The external path is here deliberately - it is a list that NARROWS, and a good case that never exercised it would leave the direction where it must NOT fire unproven. Since #1276 it also carries a `make verify` row and a Makefile defining `verify`, so the typed-subject path is exercised in the direction where it must NOT fire.

cases.name: good-accounted-data-home
cases.why: A tree whose `controls/census.md` matches it exactly, beside a decision record that carries no census table - the shape this repository has had since #1671. A gate that reads the record first parses 0 rows and refuses it (measured against the pre-#1671 gate), and this gate is in `make verify`, so that false red would block every merge. It exercises the same three accounting paths and the typed `make verify` subject as `good-accounted`.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED: the gate is new and never shipped blind, so there is no revision to vendor - `--verify-provenance` therefore reports `unverified`, which is correct and must never be read as `ok`. This is the FIRST FRAMING of the problem, on the record: #1060 as filed described the forward direction and said nothing about the extraction rule, and written straight from that sentence you get this file - every backticked token anywhere in the document counts, and there is no STALE check. It misses `bad-unaccounted` because the prose names the script, misses `bad-stale-subject` because it never looks in that direction, and agrees with the real gate on `good-accounted`, which is what makes the demonstration isolated. Since #1671 it resolves the census the way the gate does (`controls/census.md`, else the decision record), a change to WHERE it reads and not to either blindness: it must miss `bad-unaccounted-data-home` because the prose names the script, never because it could not find the file. It is constructed, so re-cutting it rewrites no history.
